hook_text: A factory loses R600 000 in ten days, and nobody touched a machine. How?
clip_script: A strike. Karoo Canning makes R60 000 of canned fruit a day. Ten days of strike: R600 000 gone. Each worker loses R400 a day, R4 000 in total. No work, no pay. So are unions bad for business? Not so fast. A union means one deal for 40 workers, not 40 arguments. Clear ways to solve complaints early. Safer factories. More training. Workers who stay. The real secret is wages and productivity together. Wages up 6 percent and output up 6 percent: the cost of each can stays the same and everyone wins. Wages up with no extra output: costs rise and jobs are at risk. Cooperation builds growth that lasts.
visual_style: A silent factory floor with a counter ticking up lost rand, then a split screen of good and bad effects, ending with two bars, wages and output, rising side by side.
pacing: A dramatic hook, a quick two-sided list, a clear closing idea.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to weigh up the effects of trade unions on business and growth.
